issues.description: Field 'abbreviation' has conflicting types between the UML/problem statement and the solution code. The UML in problem_statement.md declares Ride.abbreviation as type 'char' (problem_statement.md lines 21-24). In the solution, Ride declares a private field 'abbreviation' of type String and its constructor/public API use String (src/de/tum/in/ase/Ride.java). However, RollerCoaster and LaunchedRollerCoaster in the solution declare constructors that take a 'char abbreviation' parameter (src/de/tum/in/ase/RollerCoaster.java and src/de/tum/in/ase/LaunchedRollerCoaster.java) and pass that value to super(...). This inconsistency (char vs String) is structural: it will cause compilation errors when a char is passed to a super constructor expecting a String and confuses students which type to use for the abbreviation attribute.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of 'abbreviation' consistent across the UML/problem statement and all Java classes. Either: (A) Update the UML and all constructors/getters to use String (change UML to 'abbreviation: String') so Ride.abbreviation remains String and RollerCoaster/LaunchedRollerCoaster constructors accept String; or (B) Change the solution code so Ride.abbreviation is of type char (update Ride's field, constructor parameter and getter to char) and ensure RollerCoaster and all subclasses use char parameters and call the matching super(...) constructor. Apply the chosen change consistently to Ride, RollerCoaster, LaunchedRollerCoaster, and any other affected classes to resolve compilation errors and reduce student confusion.
